chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
From the uprightness (or Hanifism) is circumcision.

key_terms.الْحَنِيفِيَّة: Hanifyyah: The upright monotheistic tradition, specifically referring to the religion of Ibrahim (AS), characterized by pure tawhid.
key_terms.الْخِتَانُ: Khitan: Circumcision, the ritual removal of the foreskin, considered a act of purification and sunnah.

ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of circumcision in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies circumcision as a defining marker of the Hanifiyyah, the pure monotheistic tradition traced back to Prophet Ibrahim (AS). This establishes the physical act not merely as hygiene, but as a spiritual sign of fidelity to the primordial covenant. The hadith underscores the inseparable link between bodily purification and spiritual uprightness in Shia jurisprudence.
